arxiv-2007-09340.title: Determinisability of one-clock timed automata
arxiv-2007-09340.creator: Lorenzo Clemente, Sławomir Lasota, Radosław Piórkowski
arxiv-2007-09340.description: Abstract The deterministic membership problem for timed automata asks whether the timed language recognised by a nondeterministic timed automaton can be recognised by a deterministic timed automaton. We show that the problem is decidable when the input automaton is a one-clock nondeterministic timed automaton without epsilon transitions and the number of clocks of the deterministic timed automaton is fixed.

arxiv-2012-00503.title: Radiative 𝜶 𝟕 ​ 𝒎 \bm{\alpha^{7}m} QED contribution to the helium Lamb shift
arxiv-2012-00503.creator: Vojtěch Patkóš, Vladimir A. Yerokhin, Krzysztof Pachucki
arxiv-2012-00503.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Vojtěch Patkóš, Vladimir A. Yerokhin, Krzysztof Pachucki. We present a derivation of the last unknown part of the α 7 ​ m \alpha^{7}m contribution to the Lamb shift of a two-electron atom, induced by the radiative QED effects beyond the Bethe logarithm. This derivation is performed in the framework of nonrelativistic quantum electrodynamics and is valid for the triplet (spin S = 1 S=1 ) atomic states. The obtained formulas are free from any divergences and are suitable for a numerical evaluation.

arxiv-2310-03367.title: A paraxial approach for the inverse problem of vibro-acoustic imaging in frequency domain
arxiv-2310-03367.creator: Teresa Rauscher
arxiv-2310-03367.description: Abstract This paper presents a paraxial modeling approach for vibro-acoustography, a high-frequency ultrasound imaging technique that makes use of the excited low-frequency field to achieve a higher resolution while avoiding speckles. We start from a general second order wave equation, introduce a second order perturbation and make use of a paraxial change of variables to pass over to directed beams.

Scattering in complex media scrambles light, obscuring images and hindering applications ranging from astronomy to microscopy. While computational algorithms and wavefront shaping can, in principle, reverse this mixing by exploiting the near-linear nature of light propagation, in practice the inversion process is highly susceptible to limitations such as the finite number of controllable modes, noise, losses, and inaccuracies in the forward model.

pmc-10771855.description: Background and objectiveA healthy lifestyle encompasses healthy eating, regular exercise, getting enough sleep, and avoiding smoking, drug abuse, and alcohol, which will help improve mental health and manage the symptoms of anxiety, stress, and depression. In this study, we aimed to evaluate the relationship between a healthy lifestyle and psychological well-being among Saudi adolescent girls.

pmc-11410735.title: Subtle Presentation of Two Rare Gynecological Cancers in a Single Patient: A Case Report
pmc-11410735.creator: Eden Estevez, Frederick Friedman, Tiangui Huang, Nora Morgenstern
pmc-11410735.description: Yolk sac tumors (YSTs) are rare germ-cell malignancies that usually develop in the gonads. Similarly, gastric-type adenocarcinoma of the endocervix (GAS) is a rare kind of gynecological cancer that has piqued interest due to its distinctive clinical and pathological features. These two malignancies in a single patient present a unique and challenging scenario.

pmc-11466604.title: Application of knowledge graph in smart irrigation district management decision making
pmc-11466604.creator: Shaonan Sun, Yuqing Ding, Guoyu Dong, Ailing Wang
pmc-11466604.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Regarding the traditional irrigation and drainage management methods in China's irrigation districts, there are problems such as complex management processes, dispersed information systems, difficulty in resource sharing, diverse data sources, and insufficient intelligent auxiliary decision-making.

pmc-11644303.title: Spatio-Temporal Heterogeneity of Ecological Quality in a Typical Dryland of Northern China Driven by Climate Change and Human Activities
pmc-11644303.creator: Shuai Li, Junliang Gao, Pu Guo, Ge Zhang, Yu Ren, Qi Lu, Qinwen Bai, Jiahua Lu
pmc-11644303.description: With the intensification of climate change and anthropogenic impacts, the ecological environment in drylands faces serious challenges, underscoring the necessity for regionally adapted ecological quality evaluation. This study evaluates the suitability of the original Remote Sensing Ecological Index (oRSEI), modified RSEI (mRSEI), and adapted RSEI (aRSEI) in a typical dryland region of northern China.

pmc-12465853.title: miR-671-5p as a diagnostic biomarker and therapeutic target in periodontitis via THBS1 regulation
pmc-12465853.creator: Shan Huang, Wei Cheng, Jianlan Deng
pmc-12465853.description: BackgroundEarly diagnosis and therapeutic targeting of periodontitis remain challenging. This study aimed to investigate the clinical relevance and mechanistic role of miR-671-5p in pathogenesis of periodontitis.MethodsClinical data and gingival crevicular fluid (GCF) samples were collected from 78 periodontitis patients and 79 healthy controls.

pmc-12507506.title: Wandering Spleen, A Rare Cause of Acute Abdomen: A Case Report
pmc-12507506.creator: John Kanyiri Yambah, Kojo Amanfo Ninson, Abdul Samed Sulemana, Richardson Edwin Annan, Vishnu Nene Limon Abayateye, Gifty Aba Donkor, Moses Dokurugu, Ninnang Tobias
pmc-12507506.description: A wandering spleen (WS) is rare and often presents a diagnostic challenge to clinicians. We report a WS in a 16‐year‐old who presented with abdominal pain, vomiting, and peritonism. Imaging (ultrasound and CT scans), which usually facilitates a prompt diagnosis, was inconclusive, and the diagnosis was made by exploratory laparotomy.

pmc-12552654.title: Artificial intelligence strategies based on random forests for detecting ischemia–reperfusion injury changes in kidney tissue during intravital imaging
pmc-12552654.creator: Igor Pantic, Jovana Paunovic Pantic, Svetlana Valjarevic, Jelena Cumic, Peiwu Qin, Peter R Corridon
pmc-12552654.description: This study presents a supervised machine learning approach using a Random Forest classifier to detect ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) in kidney tissue based on intravital two-photon microscopy data. A rodent model of unilateral renal IRI was used, with 30 min of pedicle occlusion followed by 15 min of reperfusion.

pmc-12838024.title: Antimicrobial Resistance in Bacterial Strains of Agricultural Interest: Predictions Based on Genomic Data
pmc-12838024.creator: Eloísa Pajuelo, Manuel Medina-Rodríguez, Noris J. Flores-Duarte, Bouchra Doukkali, Jennifer Mesa-Marín, Ignacio D. Rodríguez-Llorente, Salvadora Navarro-Torre
pmc-12838024.description: Background: Plant growth promoting bacteria (PGPB) are non-pathogenic bacteria that enhance plant growth through several mechanisms such as nutrient mobilization, phytohormones production, defense against phytopathogens, and alleviation of plant stress. Hence, these bacteria are used as ecologic biofertilizers to diminish the use of agrochemicals.

pmc-12859902.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundOral transmission of Chagas disease has been registered in rural and periurban areas of South America. In Brazil, outbreaks have involved food, sugar cane juice, water, or soup contaminated with infected triatomines or their feces. Here, we report an investigation into an acute Chagas disease outbreak in a rural area of the municipality of Serrolândia, in the semi-arid region of Bahia, Brazil.MethodsWe conducted a descriptive study based on primary care information, epidemiological evaluation, entomological surveillance, and molecular analysis.

pmc-12967526.title: A phase II study of atezolizumab in combination with stereotactic radiation for patients with triple-negative breast cancer and brain metastasis
pmc-12967526.creator: Antonio Giordano, Noah Graham, Ayal A. Aizer, Nabihah Tayob, Alyssa M. Pereslete, Jonathan D. Schoenfeld, Jose Pablo Leone, Raechel Davis, Timothy K. Erick, Erica L. Mayer, Eric P. Winer, Ian Krop, Sara M. Tolaney, Nancy U. Lin
pmc-12967526.description: PurposeTriple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) patients with brain metastases have a poor prognosis and limited treatment options. Preclinical and clinical evidence suggests that radiotherapy may act synergistically with immune checkpoint inhibitors.MethodsWe conducted an open-label, single-arm, phase II study of atezolizumab plus stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) in metastatic TNBC patients with brain metastases.

pmc-13233934.title: Controlling Spatio-Temporal Sequences of Neural Activity by Local Synaptic Changes
pmc-13233934.creator: Hauke O. Wernecke, Andrew B. Lehr, Arvind Kumar
pmc-13233934.description: The neural basis of behavior is believed to consist of sequential patterns of neural activity in the relevant brain regions. Behavioral flexibility also requires neural circuit mechanisms that support dynamic control of sequential activity. However, mechanisms to control and reconfigure sequential activity have received little attention.

pmc-13568409.creator: Carlalberto Francia, Lucia Donno, Gaia Strada, Veronica Cimolin, Mario Covarrubias Rodriguez, Manuela Galli
pmc-13568409.description: Markerless video-based motion capture is a fast-developing, low-burden and versatile alternative to marker-based stereophotogrammetry, yet independent validation evidence for several commercial solutions is still scarce. This study validates the markerless software CapturyStudio (The Captury GmbH, Saarbrücken, Germany) for the reconstruction of upper- and lower-limb joint kinematics, comparing it with a validated Xsens (Movella, Henderson, NV, USA) inertial measurement unit system.

pmc-13582786.title: Unlocking the potential of gold nanoparticles with insights into green synthesis, mechanisms, characterization and multifunctional applications
pmc-13582786.creator: Hansa Gul, Nasir Assad, Zahida Nasreen, Maria kanwal, Muhammad Nauman Khan, Ahmed Vandy, Muhammad Naeem-ul-Hassan
pmc-13582786.description: Gold nanop articles (AuNPs) have garnered significant attention in biomedical research owing to their unique physicochemical properties, including biocompatibility, tunable stability, and versatile surface chemistries. However, conventional physical and chemical synthesis methods often depend on hazardous reagents and energy-intensive conditions, raising environmental and health concerns regarding their use.
